While this excerpt focuses deeply on the single perspective of the young Baron rather than multiple characters, it excels at convincingly and accurately depicting the mindset of a morally ambiguous and somewhat unappealing character. The protagonist is portrayed as a superficial "womanizer" (Frauenjäger) who avoids self-reflection, cannot stand his own company, and views women—from a friend's wife to a chambermaid—purely as prey for his next erotic conquest. Despite these objectionable traits, the author dives deeply into his psychology, explaining his motivations with great believability. By comparing him to an unlit match in a box that needs the "friction" of other people to ignite, and by detailing how his passion is that of a cold, calculating gambler rather than a lover, the narrative creates a complex, three-dimensional, and psychologically accurate portrait without endorsing his behavior.
